title: Of the different Species of Philosophy
author: David Hume
summary: The opening essay of what became Hume's Enquiry. There are two kinds of moral philosophy: the easy kind, which paints virtue in amiable colours and moves people to act, and the abstruse kind, which seeks the principles of human nature and is soon forgotten. Hume defends the second: accurate reasoning sharpens the easy philosophy and every art, and only a careful study of the understanding can drive out the false metaphysics that shelters superstition.
